about: The humidifier's mist: a fine white plume out of its top, drifting off with the air and gone within a metre as the droplets dry. Every number is this record's, after real ultrasonic humidifiers. Frame: the room's middle on its floor.

effects.name: humidifier_mist
effects.from: footage: commons-ultrasonic-humidifier, flickr-3929581537 (an ultrasonic humidifier's mist (droplets of 1 to 5 micrometres) blown out of its top in one column about 11 degrees either side and showing at least 0.16 m up (its exit speed and droplet size were not found in footage; the 0.35 to 0.6 m/s is this record's), too fine to fall, slowing, sinking a little as the cool wet plume is heavier than the room's air, and drying away within a metre)

no_light: fog, ice and steam give off no light of their own; the place's lamps light them

footage.how: Measured on each photograph's pixels against a thing of known size in it (named with each source; a typical size where the maker's own was not looked up, so to roughly a third), or read off a report's text. A plume running off the frame bounds a measure on one side only (null). The seconds are the place's own: when its motion record runs the pump and opens the door.

commons-ultrasonic-humidifier.what: an ultrasonic humidifier at work (Vitek), public domain
commons-ultrasonic-humidifier.measured: looked at on the photograph and measured on its pixels, against the humidifier's height (about 0.33 m, its maker's listing for the current model): the plume shows at least 0.16 m, running off the top; 9 mm wide at the nozzle and 57 mm 0.15 m up, about 11 degrees either side; one continuous column
